result:
final.py scores **about 86–87 on the search split**, roughly 85× faster than the reference, using **10 of the 24 scorer calls**. It matched the reference exactly on 3 harness seeds I never tuned on and on about 2,000 small edge-case inputs.

I couldn't run a held-out check, because the scorer only exposes the search split. The final score on unseen instances is still to come.

**Budget:** I announced the default ~15 minutes but stopped after about 7 by the system clock, with 14 calls left. That's earlier than the skill asks: the scores had levelled off within the scorer's ~±3% noise.

| | Search score |
|---|---|
| Baseline | ~1.0 |
| First champion (c1) | 70.1 |
| **Final pick (c12 = final.py)** | **87.2, 86.2 on a rescore** |

**Why it's faster:**
- **Identical word sets are grouped first.** Every pair inside a group is reported directly, and each distinct set is compared only once.
- **Prefix filtering replaces the all-pairs loop.** Words are put in one global order, rarest first, and sets are processed from smallest to largest. Two sets that are at least 80% alike must share a word among the first `n − ⌈0.8n⌉ + 1` words of each set. So each set only looks up that short start of its list in an index of words to sets. The index only stores the shorter start that the size limit allows (`n − ⌈8n/9⌉ + 1`).
- **Candidates are checked exactly** with the reference's rule (`9·|A∩B| ≥ 4·(|A|+|B|)`), after first dropping any set smaller than `⌈0.8n⌉`.
- **Short sets skip most of the work.** A set of 4 or fewer words can only match a larger set or an identical one. So it isn't looked up at all, and only its rarest word is indexed (via `min`, with no sort). This gave the last ~5%, which suggests the search data has many short records.

**Approaches tried:**
- Ordering words alphabetically instead of by frequency was 27× slower on my harness, because common words fill the prefixes. Dropped.
- Skipping words that appear in only one set (c8) was neutral on both my harness and the scorer.
- Removing the `collections` import to save import time (c6, c11) was a tie, within noise.
- Importing a private counting helper (c5) was rejected by the scorer's static check, which cost one call.

It also stays correct and fast on hostile inputs: a 20-word vocabulary was 5× faster than the reference and records of 40–120 words were 15× faster.

**Candidate log** (`calls left: 14`):

| Candidate | Change | Harness (2 × 3,000 records) | Search score | Kept? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1 | prefix filter + identical-set grouping | 21.3 ms | 70.1 | superseded |
| c2 | shorter index prefix | 19.0 ms | — | superseded |
| c3 | precomputed word ranks + `Counter` | 18.0 ms | 79.3 | superseded |
| c4 | alphabetical order | 494 ms | — | dropped |
| c5 | private import | — | rejected | dropped |
| c6 | manual counting, no imports | 19.0 ms | 76.4 | tie, dropped |
| c7 | faster split and grouping | 17.9 ms | — | folded into c9 |
| c8 | skip words in only one set | 19.4 ms | 76.8 | dropped |
| c9 | c7 + one merged lookup/index loop | 17.7 ms | 83.6, 81.5 | parent |
| c10 | per-size constant tables | ±0 | — | dropped |
| c11 | c9 without imports | — | 81.8 | tie |
| c12 | min-only path for sets of 4 or fewer words | 17.7 ms | 87.2, 86.2 | **final** |

Everything is in `eval/loop-bench/runs/r28/s2/dedup/`: `final.py`, `harness.py`, `bench.py`, `c1.py`–`c12.py`, and `calls.log`, which the score script writes.
